correctness.rationale: The generator gives an exact coercive quadratic Lyapunov drift and a synchronous mean-square contraction, proving stationary existence and uniqueness. Exact stationary quadratic equations yield a,b,c; for linear observables conditional means evolve with A, hence K(t)=exp(At)C. Its antisymmetric off-diagonal factor is exactly -2/[gamma(r+2)+1] and the matrix exponential gives the claimed difference of decaying exponentials. Root ordering, positivity and a unique peak follow algebraically. Right first and second derivatives give s and gamma inverse explicitly; the probe-only zero-lag variance and right slope separately determine r and gamma. All parameter domains, noise factors, and time boundaries were checked. The bundled standard-library verifier passed 575 finite checks; this is corroboration only, not a universal proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 same-model source supplies the probe/bath SDE, resetting generator and stationary moment equations, but its inspected model/moment analysis treats equal-time moments and limiting densities; the assessed strict all-lag antisymmetry, unique lag extremum, and two distinct inverse maps from right-jet data are not in the examined source text. The 2024/2025 renewed-GLE treatment and the abstract of the Goswami 2025 selectively reset coupled-bath model has two-time probe autocorrelations, not a retained auxiliary bath under partial state resetting with directional cross-lag inverse map. The exact general semigroup principle is acknowledged and not called novel. Targeted literature and research-record searches did not locate equivalent formulas. Residual risk remains from full-text search limitations and possible general reset-OU treatment; independent priority review is still needed.
residual_risks: Complete uninterrupted text of the identical-model 2026 article was not accessible; an uninspected equation or appendix could contain a closely related two-time result.

The asymmetry formula is derived by elementary finite-dimensional matrix algebra once the stationary second moments are known; value rests on the sign/unique-peak/inverse interpretation, not on novel matrix techniques.

value.rationale: Cross-time directionality is a natural measurement of nonequilibrium memory retained when the observable probe is reset but its environment is not. The all-lag sign and unique delay maximum specify a nontrivial response profile, while both a bath-assisted and a probe-only inverse map identify a hidden relaxation rate exactly using second-order time data. This directly addresses the source model’s physical control parameter and is neither an arbitrary parameter slice nor merely a numerical increment. No claims are made about finite-sample robustness or experimental validation; reconstructing derivatives from noisy data may be difficult.
